name: Nasdaq-100
basis: QQQ gross-total-return proxy expressed on the matching-date XYZ100 perp point scale; perp history ends at its latest raw price

fundingForecast.displaySign: positive is earned by a perp long; negative is paid by a perp long

onchainSpot.preferenceBasis: all pages display separate CEX reported-volume and contract-backed DEX execution sections
onchainSpot.volumeSource: direct Binance, Bitget, Bybit, OKX, and Meteora venue APIs plus factory-verified PancakeSwap V3 pool-event volume indexed by DexScreener; DEX quote routes without indexed pool-event volume are excluded
onchainSpot.liquiditySource: direct CEX order books; direct Ethereum, Robinhood-chain, and PancakeSwap V3 quoter depth; direct Meteora pool state; and direct Jupiter executable round-trip quotes

peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: NVDA 19.3% with 3/3 replicate support; MSFT 15.7% with 3/3 replicate support; AAPL 14.0% with 3/3 replicate support; AMZN 11.0% with 3/3 replicate support; SP500 25.0% with 2/3 replicate support; GOOGL 8.0% with 2/3 replicate support; META 7.0% with 2/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is one of the largest Nasdaq-100 constituents and a central driver of the index's artificial intelligence and semiconductor return exposure, so its earnings and risk sentiment have outsized influence on XYZ100 performance.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft is a core mega-cap Nasdaq-100 weight with large cloud, software, and AI exposure, making it one of the closest single-name return comparators to the index.

peers.name: Apple
peers.reason: Apple is another dominant Nasdaq-100 constituent whose hardware cycle, services monetization, and mega-cap growth profile materially shape index-level returns.

peers.name: Amazon
peers.reason: Amazon combines consumer technology and cloud infrastructure exposure, both of which are important Nasdaq-100 return engines, so it is a closer peer than remote cyclical or commodity proxies.

peers.name: S&P 500
peers.reason: It is the closest broad index comparator because the Nasdaq-100's largest constituents are also among the largest S&P 500 weights, so it captures the shared U.S. equity and mega-cap technology return engine.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: Alphabet is a leading Nasdaq-100 growth platform whose digital advertising and cloud businesses map closely to the index's concentrated technology and communication exposure.

peers.name: Meta Platforms
peers.reason: Meta is a major constituent tied to digital advertising and AI-driven platform spending, both important return drivers for the target index.

primary_index_hedge.name: S&P 500
primary_index_hedge.reason: The S&P 500 is the primary hedge because it is the dominant systematic index for US equities and captures the broad market beta that drives most Nasdaq-100 movement, while being less concentrated in mega-cap technology than the target itself.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

underlierSelection.method: highest summed live contract volume; open interest and contract count break ties

model.name: ATM-straddle-implied lognormal distribution
model.description: Each target uses the nearest paired liquid ATM call and put. Their combined ask implies the expiration distribution shown on the chart.
model.measure: option-implied, not a historical or physical forecast
